meeting.body: Maui County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee
meeting.summary: At a Kīhei budget hearing, residents raised Wailuku water rates, Cove Park wastewater, eviction mediation and disaster recovery funding.
meeting.recap: The Budget, Finance, Economic Development Committee held a budget hearing in Kīhei.[[0:01:30]] The only agenda item was the County's fiscal year 27 budget.[[0:03:48]] A rider said they depend on the MEO Handy Van for doctor visits and shopping.[[0:10:16]] A resident asked questions about a planned desalination plant, which removes salt from water.[[0:20:34]] A testifier said the damaged Wailuku water system's owner offered to sell it for $13 million.[[0:26:48]] The testifier said Wailuku Water told farmers it may double or triple their water rates.[[0:30:56]] He asked for $5 million more to buy back wetlands to help with flooding.[[0:41:27]] Maui Mediation Services said it received 82 eviction notices in March.[[1:29:03]] A disaster case manager said a long-term recovery group now serves all disasters but has no funds for that.[[2:05:15]] A councilmember asked why contractors who took rebuilders' money are not named publicly.[[2:06:10]] The meeting adjourned at 8:10.[[2:10:52]]
meeting.next: The County Department of Ag asked farmers for their old and new water invoices to compare rates. Member Cook offered to talk with a testifier after the meeting. The disaster case manager said the recovery group will ask the Council for help funding its work on all disasters.

issues.oneLine: A long-term recovery group said its mission now covers all disasters, not just the wildfires.
issues.why: A councilmember said new rebuilders keep getting ripped off by the same licensed contractor.
issues.next: The disaster case manager said the group will ask the Council for funding help.
issues.brief: The disaster case manager said the group helped complete two homes (hale) in Lahaina.[[#1]] The group's disaster case management program works directly with homeowners to help them rebuild.[[#2]] A councilmember asked why contractors who took rebuilders' money are not named publicly.[[#3]] The disaster case manager said the state consumer agency (DCCA) was involved and legal steps are in process.[[#4]]
